name: postselect-sched
description: The many-worlds sorter as a schedulable primitive. The visitor's claim (postselection reads the optimum in O(1), cost = depreciation of the other universes) was already adjudicated CONDITIONAL-WALL in bqp-map exp6. This prototype promotes it from a certificate row to a theorem layer: the depreciation ledger is a Las Vegas restart strategy, and nobody has machine-verified that layer — Luby-Sinclair-Zuckerman restart theory (optimal fixed cutoff, no-beating by any strategy, universal doubling within O(lambda log lambda)) is all pen-and-paper. Delivered here: (T1) sorter branch algebra with the filter-not-channel audit (conditioning is affine only in the branch-weighted sense, trace-distance 1/6 certificate instance; Kraus completeness); (T2) restart algebra two-path machine-checked (renewal sum vs closed lambda), exhaustive no-beating at small depth in BOTH cost models (early-stop credit and always-pay), universal doubling strategy within the LSZ93 theorem-5 bound on three families, and the Grover-threshold law: pure postselection is restart-optimal iff the marked density t/N exceeds c* (machine-measured, binding at k=1: c* = (3-sqrt(2))/4 asymptotically); (T3) counting power: conditional outcome probabilities are exact #P-fraction values against an integer referee, odd-denominator gap separation and the single-shot decision error law; (T4) the scheduling contact: postselection is a FREE resource exactly when the environment heralds the same branch rejection (identical geometric waiting law, query column exactly zero), and the online depth-doubling schedule for unknown marked count t stays within a small factor of the oracle-optimal restart
